headline: Readiness is red across the board this morning — today's long run stays easy, no marathon/threshold segments.
body_state: Training readiness **23** (Garmin) / **28.8** (composite, band **low**), driven by sleep: last night was **4.8h** (17,220s), sleep score **54**, on top of **23h of 14-day sleep debt** already building. HRV sits **below your normal band** (37ms last night). Body battery is **32** — under the 40 threshold where quality sessions reliably underperform. Load is also spiking: **ACWR 2.02** (>1.5 carries 2–4x next-week injury risk), TSB **-18.1**. This is the fourth straight day of near-daily indoor cardio classes (Aug 4 RPE 8, Aug 5 evening RPE 8, Aug 6 RPE 6) stacked on top of running mileage — exactly the load-compounding pattern flagged in yesterday's analysis, and it's now shown up as today's crash.
session: The plan has today down as an **8km Progressive Long Run** (4.7km easy → 2.4km marathon pace → 0.8km threshold), and the plan's own note already anticipated this: check readiness before leaning into the fast segments. It's still low. Run it **easy-only** — hold 4:35–5:03/km for the full 8km and skip the marathon/threshold portions; the aerobic volume covers today's stimulus and the specificity work waits for the next quality day once HRV and sleep recover. If body battery hasn't visibly climbed by the time you're out the door, cutting the distance back is also fine — nothing forces the full 8km on a 32-battery morning.
recent: Three cardio classes in four days (Aug 4, 5-evening, 6) with two RPE-8s stacked on an already-scheduled Aug 5 easy run — the Aug 6 analysis called this out directly and linked it to the readiness step-down you're seeing today. The one clean data point was Tuesday's 5km easy run: HR stayed at 67% max despite a 4:32/km pace, so it was genuinely easy physiologically even though it logged RPE 6 — the fatigue is coming from the cardio classes, not the running. Cadence on that run was 155spm with a 271ms GCT, still the overstriding pattern flagged in prior reviews.
focus: Protect today: easy-only running, no new hard work until HRV and sleep are back in range.
Stop stacking hard cardio classes onto scheduled run days — pick one per day, not both.
Once readiness clears, start folding station-specific work (Row 1000m, Sandbag Lunges, Sled Pull) into the cardio slots instead of unstructured intervals.
